# Demos {#sec-demos}

The demo scripts are found in the `scripts/` directory. They are meant to be
read and run by a person, so they use `print`. They are not part of the library.
Each script prints a readable result for one stage of the pipeline.

A script is run with the `M` variable.

```bash
make demo M=transpiler
make demo M=translator
make demo M=simulator
make demo M=vectorizer
make demo M=metrics
make demo M=compile
make demo M=adder
```

## The shared helpers {.unnumbered}

The file `scripts/_common.py` holds the helpers that the demos share.

| Function | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `make_info(entangler)` | Builds a synthetic `BackendInfo` for the given entangler. |
| `bell()` | Builds the Bell circuit. |
| `ghz3()` | Builds the GHZ circuit. |

## `demo_transpiler.py` {.unnumbered}

The provider information and the transpiled circuit are printed for each local
backend: the `BasicSimulator`, a Heron-like backend, an Eagle-like backend and a
fake unknown backend.

## `demo_translator.py` {.unnumbered}

The native operation list of the Bell and GHZ circuits is printed, for both the
MS and the ZZ entangler. The count of each gate type is also printed.

## `demo_simulator.py` {.unnumbered}

A table is printed. There is one row per step and per qubit, and the values
`(r, theta, phi)` are given in degrees for the angles.

## `demo_vectorizer.py` {#sec-demo-vectorizer}

The same table is printed, but with the Cartesian values `(x, y, z)` and with the
probability `p(|1⟩)`.

## `demo_metrics.py` {.unnumbered}

A table is printed with the operation, the accumulated fidelity, the per-qubit
fidelities, the inactivity, the vibration and the accumulated cost.

## `demo_compile.py` {.unnumbered}

The full pipeline is run for the Bell and GHZ circuits. Two files are written:
`out/bell.json` and `out/ghz3.json`. The `out` directory is ignored by Git. The
files can be opened with the [basic viewer](../frontend/viewer.qmd).

## `demo_adder.py` {.unnumbered}

The QFT adder is built and compiled. The Fourier matrix is printed for two
qubits, and the adder is run for three input pairs. One JSON file is written for
each pair, for example `out/adder_n2_1_1.json`. The example is described on the
[QFT adder](../examples/qft-adder.qmd) page.

## `package_qollab.py` {.unnumbered}

This script is run with `make qollab`. The viewer, the way it is built and the rules for changing it
are on the [viewer on Qollab](../frontend/qollab.qmd) page.

The whole repository has more files than Qollab accepts (100 per project), and
Qollab looks only at the files of the root to decide the type of the project. The
script therefore builds the folder `qollab/` (not committed) with a complete **JS
project**: `index.html`, `main.css` and `main.js` made from the viewer, `qollab_api.py`,
`requirements.txt` and the libraries `backend/` and `examples/`. `main.py` is left
out, because in a JS project it could compile a second time and spend a second
IonQ job. The content of the folder is uploaded to Qollab. See
`documentation/prompts/qollab_pruebas.md`.

## `generate_outputs.py` {.unnumbered}

This script is run with `make outputs`, not with `make demo`. It compiles a
small set of circuits, including two 16-qubit performance circuits, writes the
JSON files to `out/`, and writes `out/manifest.json` for the viewer. See the
[Performance circuits](../examples/performance.qmd) page.
